generic_domain.justification: Probabilistic models encompass a wide range of statistical techniques that use probability distributions to represent uncertainty in data. They include various specific types such as Bayesian networks, Markov models, and others. 'Probabilistic modeling' refers more generally to the practice of using these models, while 'probabilistic models' is the broader category. Thus, 'probabilistic models' serves as a comprehensive umbrella term that can cover all aspects within probabilistic methodologies.
